newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Horta says he has fresh Timor torture evidence.
newsitem.headline: Horta says he has fresh Timor torture evidence.

text.p: Nobel Peace laureate Jose Ramos Horta, the exiled East Timor leader, said on Sunday he would show the United Nations what he said was fresh evidence of widespread torture in the Indonesian-ruled territory.

He told Reuters by telephone from Geneva that he would present on Tuesday to Bacre Waly Ndiaye, the U.N. special rapporteur on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions, a video of photographs he said had been smuggled out of East Timor showing youths being tortured by Indonesian soldiers.
"It shows a pattern of systematic, gross, widespread human rights violations. If anything it shows it is not isolated... This is evidence of a pattern of the most brutal kind," he said.

Indonesia, which invaded the former Portuguese territory in 1975 and annexed it the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations, has consistently denied allegations of torture and other human rights abuses in East Timor.
The pictures show khaki-clad men apparently torturing young men using sticks, chairs, electric shocks and chains. In one sequence two youths are tied to a tree and apparently hit with a shovel.
Another appears to shows bodies being buried in a shallow grave before being burned.
It was impossible to independently authenticate the pictures.

Horta, who won the Nobel peace prize last year jointly with respected East Timorese bishop Carlos Belo, said he believed the pictures were genuine. He said church sources had recently smuggled the pictures out of mainly Roman Catholic East Timor.
East Timorese sources said they believed the pictures had been taken in or around the north-eastern town of Baucau between October 1995 and December 1996.
A year ago the Melbourne-based East Timor Human Rights Centre released photographs to the Australian media showing what they said were four Timorese youths being tortured by the Indonesian military.
